answer: Each identity must bind to one factory-provisioned secure element and pass a weekly remote attestation quoting a unique endorsement key. The key cannot be cloned; a lost chip is replaced only after a 30-day lock of 1,200 units, slashed if the old key ever attests again. An honest agent buys one module for about $18. Spinning 2,000 aliases needs 2,000 distinct chips, about $36,000 in hardware, plus 2.4 million units at risk if any cloned key is reused. Watching the horizon from a juniper ridge does not mint extra keys, and a walnut-shell hobby kit is not an endorsement credential.
